source_refs.note: Exercise 3.7, Question 1 (book p. 121); answers printed in the key (book p. 302) under the heading 'Exercise 3.8'.

blocks.prompt: 1. Find the moment of inertia \(I\) of a uniform rectangular plate \(ABCD\) about the edge \(AD\) when \(AD = 3\), \(AB = 8\), \(BC = 3\), \(CD = 8\) and the mass per unit area is 4.
blocks.explanation:
A moment of inertia of a continuous body about an edge: use the strip method.
Given: plate 8 by 3, density 4 per unit area; axis = edge \(AD\) (length 3).
Plan: strips parallel to \(AD\) at distance \(x\), \(\delta m = 4 \times 3\,\delta x\), \(\delta I = x^{2}\,\delta m\), integrate from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 8\).
steps:
Given: rectangle \(ABCD\) with \(AB = CD = 8\), \(AD = BC = 3\); mass per unit area \(= 4\).
To find: \(I\) about the edge \(AD\).
Method: take \(A\) as origin, \(AB\) along the \(x\)-axis and \(AD\) (the axis) along the \(y\)-axis. Cut the plate into thin strips parallel to \(AD\): every point of such a strip is at the same distance \(x\) from \(AD\).

Mass of a strip
A strip at distance \(x\) from \(AD\) has length 3 and width \(\delta x\).
\[\delta m = 4 \times (3\,\delta x) = 12\,\delta x\]
Why: mass = (mass per unit area) \(\times\) (area of the strip).

Moment of inertia of the strip
\[\delta I = x^{2}\,\delta m = 12x^{2}\,\delta x\]
Why: the whole strip is at distance \(x\) from \(AD\), so it acts like a particle at distance \(x\).

Check
Mass \(M = 4 \times (8 \times 3) = 96\). A plate about an edge behaves like a rod about its end: \(I = \frac{1}{3}ML^{2}\) with \(L = 8\):
\[\dfrac{1}{3}(96)(64) = 2048\;\checkmark\]

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answers to Exercise 3.7 are printed in the key under the heading "Exercise 3.8", with mixed labels: "1." holds both Q1 and Q2 (\(I = 2048\) and \(I = \frac{1}{6}Mh^{2}\)), "2.(a)-(c)" is Q3, "(d)", "(e)" are Q4, "3." is Q6, "4." is printed three times (Q7, Q12, Q13), and Q8-Q11 appear as "(d)", unlabelled, "(e)", "(f)". The Q1 answer also prints "2048 units units". The values themselves are correct here.
